description: pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:1235-1279: verify_ocsp_responder constructs NoCheckShim wrapping the caller's revocation checker, then passes `&shim` to verify_chain. If the chain[0] (responder cert) carries id-pkix-ocsp-nocheck AND the chain is incomplete and the wrapper hardcodes `&NoAiaFetcher` (line 1273), AIA won't fire — but the OCSP wrapper also doesn't expose an AiaFetcher parameter, so a chain like [responder-with-nocheck-but-missing-intermediate] always returns Aia(FetchingDisabled). That's a documented limitation. The real issue is more subtle: LeafIdent::matches uses BYTE-equality on Name (derived PartialEq on x509_cert::name::Name) per the comment at line 1352-1359. The comment claims this is safe because 'both sides come from the same DER encoder.' That holds in the fast path (chain[0] is identity-equal to itself when fed into run_revocation_checks). BUT in any future code path where validate_path is followed by revocation on a different cert object (e.g. a built chain where chain[0] could in principle be re-encoded), byte equality could miss. Today this is fine; it is a latent invariant. Trigger: future refactor that re-clones chain[0] through a path that re-encodes; nocheck bypass silently stops working. Recommend: compare via pkix_path::names_match for the Name field and bytewise on the serial (same as it does now), to make the match robust against any future re-encoding. The serial check is already opaque-bytewise; the issuer should use names_match for the same reason verify_responder_is_delegated_by does.
notes: Crypto-security framing (from /review-crypto-security pass, 2026-05-14): the OCSP-nocheck bypass is a security-critical override — if `LeafIdent::matches` returns true incorrectly, revocation is silently skipped on the wrong cert. Today the byte-equality is correct because (1) `verify_chain` propagates the exact same `&chain[0]` reference through to the shim's callback, and (2) `pkix-path` does not re-canonicalize `Certificate` values. The safety therefore depends on an invariant in another crate. Switch to `pkix_path::names_match` for the issuer DN field and keep byte-equality on the SerialNumber (which RFC 5280 §4.1.2.2 specifies as a byte-opaque INTEGER); document the rationale in the rustdoc so the security argument is visible. P1 from API-idiom lens; from a security lens this is a P2 defense-in-depth (current behavior is correct, but the safety isn't local).
title: LeafIdent uses byte-equality on Name; use names_match for robustness
